title: Brave Peckul
text: “Um… I heard a message saying it hid the key to going further inside the labyrinth, so go back and get it.”
“It came with a very thoughtful explanation too—something about it playing back in the voice of the person’s most beloved member of the opposite sex.”
“Right. Though I have to wonder about the voice switching partway through.”
“Was that how it was for you, Naofumi-san?”
“Itsuki’s stayed the same? Motoyasu-kun too, I bet.”

“The ‘opposite sex’ part was the sticking point, wasn’t it. If it really plays the voice of someone’s beloved, Motoyasu-san’s probably getting confused between someone named Filo and Naofumi-san’s voice.”
Ohhh! Filo-tan! Wherever could you be, I say! Gah… it’s maddening that I cannot proceed any further, indeed.
“Ren, whose voice did you hear? Wyndia-chan, right? Or was it Éclair-san?”
“Why those two, of all people? That’s some other-world version of me you’re thinking of.”
“Ah… Rafumi-san, then. No, wait, Luna-san.”
“I said that’s not it! In the first place, I didn’t hear any voice like that at all!”
While I was busy searching for Filo-tan, Father and the others were having quite the conversation, I say.
“Poor Ren-san, not having anyone he loves most.”
“True… if he doesn’t find someone somewhere, he’s going to end up as the lonely alchemist, Dr. Azott.”
“Stop using me as material for your jokes! Just because I didn’t hear the voice of someone I like doesn’t mean you get to tease me about it!”
“Filo-taaan!”
I do wish to hear more of your voice, indeed. Buoom! Just then, a seven-colored glowing hole appeared, shining as if to say “this is the exit.” Surely, entering there must be the answer, I say!
“Filo-taaan! Here I come, indeed!”
“Motoyasu-kun, stop!”
“Fubeh!?”
Father skillfully caught the back of my collar with a flipper just as I was about to dive into the exit, indeed.
“Why, Father, why!”

“Just calm down, Motoyasu-kun. Like it said earlier, that voice was a message that speaks in the voice of whoever’s most beloved opposite-sex person the listener has. And from what I gathered, if you go in through that hole, you’ll end up back at the entrance and have to start all over, so hold on a second.”
Ohh, so that was the reason, I see. In other words, it must simply be an exit.

“Well, that’s enough teasing Ren for now… I wonder how far this gimmick’s going to go, demanding a second loop and all… that’s the sort of thing you see in old action games, right? A second playthrough with jacked-up difficulty. Might be something like that. Like, ‘do a second loop to see the ending’…”
“Honestly, ‘there was something you missed, go back and find it’ is the kind of thing I’d rather not deal with. Though, thinking seriously about why Ren didn’t hear a voice…”
“Isn’t it simply because Ren’s the one holding the coelacanth model? We were taking turns carrying it.”
“That’d be it, I suppose. The message must have triggered because he went ahead before the person who met the condition did.”
“Alright, Ren. I’ll carry it, so let’s go find out whose voice you hear.”
“No thanks. If we can move forward without hearing some voice, that’s fine by me.”
I, for one, would still like to hear a bit more of Filo-tan’s voice, indeed.
“You’re being pretty stubborn about this, Ren-san. Are you sure you won’t regret not listening?”
“I won’t! Now come on, let’s go!”

And so, as if seizing the moment, Ren took up the coelacanth model and pressed forward—whereupon the wall that had been blocking our path vanished, letting us reach the door at last. The coelacanth model gave a glow, and with a great rumbling GOGOGO…, the door slid open upward.
“Now then… I wonder what’s beyond this. Hopefully it’s not some hidden boss we need to clear before we can get back.”
“Simply being able to go back would be best. Some kind of medicine working would be fine too.”
“Finally, the dungeon’s almost over.”
“I do wish to see Filo-tan, I say.”

Well, at least I got to hear her voice, so it wasn’t all bad, indeed. And so… what lay beyond was a chamber emblazoned with crests resembling the weapons of the Four Cardinal Heroes. In the center sat a box with a fish-shaped plate embedded in it.
“…Wait, is that seriously it? No mechanism to send us back or anything?”
“All that effort for nothing!? Are you telling me we picked the wrong dungeon to enter!?”
“I wonder. More importantly, what’s with this plate embedded in the box?”
“The fish part is what bugs me. Naofumi-san, you might be able to remove it. It seems like the sort of game-ish gimmick that’d show up.”
“Well… it does seem that way. We saw similar things along the way too.”
Just as Father stepped into the box to try examining the plate—BAM—the box suddenly slammed shut, indeed.
“Father!?”
“Whoa!? What is this!?”
Right after, with a rumbling GOGOGO…, part of the wall began rising up, I say.
“Ah, it just closed on me, I should be able to get right back out.”
Just as Father tried to open the box and climb out, the rising wall sank back down.
“Naofumi, stay in the box. There’s some kind of mechanism at work.”
“It seems there’s a gimmick involved, so please wait inside the box.”
“Eh? Wait a—”

BAM. Ren and Itsuki shut Father back inside the box, indeed. Father, are you all right? Just in case, I’ll wedge my spear into the box so he can get out. If it comes to it, I’ll smash the box open and rescue Father, I say. Before long, as the wall rose fully, a mural was revealed. It appeared to be… some kind of map of Cal Mira Island…
“A map of Cal Mira Island, I take it?”
“But… there’s one too many islands.”
“So there is.”

Besides the main island, Cal Mira had four surrounding islands—yet the map depicted a fifth, separate island as well, indeed. And it seemed there was some sort of shrine there. Come to think of it… Father and Itsuki had mentioned something about an underwater shrine, its location revealed by guidance from a large Filolial-sama.
“A hero goes to the fifth island… and when the fairies bearing the Four Cardinal Weapons leave the labyrinth…”
“It seems the spell we’re after is here, then. How do we even get to this fifth island, though?”

With a GOGOGO…, once the wall had risen fully, an adjacent picture appeared beside what we’d taken for mere mural decoration, indeed. Before a totem pole set upon an island monument, heroes bearing the Four Cardinal Weapons were shown giving each other shoulder rides in unison. At that, the island shook and released some kind of aura. From there, it seemed to connect to the island picture from before.
“…In other words. If you know this gimmick, standing before the island’s totem pole and doing the shoulder-ride thing in the right order opens up the labyrinth we’re after!”
“Game knowledge! You’d better tell us properly! Even back in the game days, this kind of convoluted gimmick would’ve been obvious, right!?”
Ren and Itsuki were shouting up at the ceiling, indeed.

“Did anyone figure something out? I’d really like to get out of this box already. Or is the deal that I need to burst out of here and introduce myself as Brave Peckul? Like… some kind of ‘surprise, the prize was a hero all along’ type of thing?”
“Never mind Naofumi-san’s joke this time, it’s fine for you to come out now.”
“Really?”
Father opened the box from the inside and stepped out, and the mural immediately sank down and disappeared from view, indeed.
“So, did you figure anything out?”

“Yes, it seems there’s another dungeon, and the means to get back to what we’re after lies there. To enter, apparently you do the shoulder-carrying thing in front of the island’s totem pole, matched up correctly.”
“Wow… so going full gag-mode turned out to be the right answer after all… we should’ve just done that when we first arrived on the island.”
“Never did I imagine I’d end up thinking we should’ve indulged Naofumi-san’s brain-jokes more seriously.”
“What a pain. If we hadn’t known, we’d have had no idea which place to prioritize going to—though either way, there was a good chance we’d have ended up here regardless.”
The outcome wouldn’t have changed, I say. In the end, we were bound to clear this place anyway, indeed.
“So… all that’s left is to head back, but it’s not going to turn out that everyone on the island’s been turned into some kind of pioneer-creature END when we return, right?”
“That’s the thing you were talking about earlier on the way here, isn’t it. What reference is that this time?”
“Hmm… I guess it just looked kind of like A Baoa Qu.”
“I can only pray that Naofumi-san’s game knowledge doesn’t end up actually connecting to this world here. Anyway, let’s head back.”
And so, with that, we returned to the vortex meant for going back and stepped inside, indeed. Round and round and round it went.
“If this were an arcade game, I feel like the staff roll would start playing right about now. Same with a lot of freeware games too.”
“Right, right. I imagine the sight of us drifting along like this must look pretty whimsical and surreal. What am I supposed to do with this feeling of utter deflation?”
“We know the goal now, so there’s nothing to do but go.”
“Ren-san. Just to raise the possibility—what if clearing the dungeon ahead is only the beginning, and we end up having to make the rounds of every activation site there is?”
“Itsuki, keep quiet! If that turns out to be true, I don’t think I could handle it!”
And so, in that manner… the swirling scenery shifted, and it felt as though we were descending from high above Cal Mira Island, far, far up in the sky.
